input.question: Why are we able to cross our eyes and unable to do the opposite?
input.ground_truth: Some people can do just that. Otherwise, it just fucks with your brain trying to put two images from both eyes at different angles together. Crossing out eyes focuses on something in front of us. Making the eyes look in their own direction doesn't do us any good for survival, so the skill never really evolved

Okay! Imagine your eyes are like two balloons on the ends of a string. You can pull the string and make the balloons (your eyes) meet in the middle—that's when you cross your eyes!

But you can't make your eyes go the other way, far away from each other, because your eyes are connected by muscles and skin. They can only move so much before they bump into your nose or just can't go any farther. So, you can cross your eyes (bring them together), but you can't push them apart really far.

It's like your eyes like to be close friends and sit together, but they don't like to run away from each other too much!
